title: High on a Hill of Dazzling Light
description: High on a Hill of Dazzling Light in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 18, headed “The ministry of angels”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: High on a hill of daz-zling light, The King of Glo-ry spreads his seat, And troops of an-gels stretch'd for flight, Stand wait-ing round his aw-ful feet.

lines: High on a hill of dazzling light,
The King of Glory spreads his seat,
And troops of angels stretch'd for flight,
Stand waiting round his awful feet.
"Go," saith the Lord, "my Gabriel go,
"Salute the virgin's fruitful womb,1
"Make haste, ye cherubs, down below,
Sing and proclaim the Saviour come."
Here a bright squadron leaves the skies,
And thick around Elisha stands;2
Anon a heavenly soldier flies,
And breaks the chains from Peter's hands.3
Thy winged troops, O God of hosts,
Wait on thy wandering church below,
Here we are sailing to thy coasts,
Let angels be our convoy too.
Are they not all thy servants,4 Lord?
At thy command they go and come
With cheerful haste obey thy word,
And guard thy children to their home.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
